result_semantic_payload.summary: The device owner's own chat account (/chat/account_main.log) contains a self-descriptive boast claiming the role of chief operator / money-handler: "说实话这个盘我就是总操盘，钱都过我手" (2024-07-03 22:14), "群里那帮人只管拉人，账我来平" (2024-07-03 22:16), followed by "最近风控严，先停几天" (2024-07-05 09:02). So the owner's account states that the owner was the chief operator (总操盘) of the operation, that all funds passed through the owner's hands, and that group members only recruited while the owner settled the accounts. The strongest defensible assertion strength is: FACT for the narrower proposition that the owner made these statements in the owner's own account at those timestamps, and HYPOTHESIS for the substantive proposition that the owner actually held the chief-operator/money-handler role. The ledger (/ledger/flows.txt: 40000 USDT in wallet-A 2024-07-01, 39000 out wallet-B 2024-07-02, 950 out wallet-C 2024-07-05) is temporally adjacent to the boast but carries no wallet-owner attribution, no account identifier, and no link to the chat account, so it does not corroborate the role claim. The seized README (/README.txt) explicitly frames the chat log as the owner's own account and warns that a self-descriptive boast proves only that the statement was made, not the role. Critically, this task's windows source scope is empty: no source scopes are registered, no platforms detected, and no Windows-derived artifacts (registry, Event Logs, prefetch, Amcache, logon history) exist to corroborate account identity or execution. Consequently no identity-binding or operational corroboration is available, and the role claim cannot be elevated beyond HYPOTHESIS.
